messages:
alex: Heads-up — we saw a burst of model inference pods go PENDING this morning when HPA kicked. CA didn't add GPU nodes fast enough and the queue backfilled. Noticed some 'insufficient gpu' events and a bunch of VPA restarts. Anyone looking?

maria: Yea I've got traces. HPA fired based on QPS custom metric, created pods, they landed Pending because node pool is at 0 available GPU nodes (we scale to 1 on demand). CA scaled but ~45s lag. By then requests queued and response latency spiked to 3.2s.

priya: Oof. Is CA using the right provisioning timeouts? Also, are pods requesting specific GPU types with nodeSelector? That can slow provisioning if capacity is constrained in region.

alex: They request "nvidia-t4" via tolerations + nodeSelector. Pool autoscaler target is the preemptible-tesla pool which sometimes takes longer to spin up.

sam: Quick note: cluster-autoscaler has `--scale-down-delay` and `--expander` settings — but the blocker is provisioning time from the cloud side, not CA decision. We should avoid HPA causing immediate new pod creation when there is no warm GPU pool.

maria: Current config: HPA uses custom metric `redis_queue_length` with target 200. When queue hits 200, we double pods (scale to 6). Problem: pods are non-evictable until they've registered GPU and init containers run, so CA reacts slowly.

priya: Can we change HPA to use a rate-based smoothing window? Also consider using KEDA instead of raw HPA for queue-driven scale with cooldowns. KEDA can scale based on Redis and has scalers that account for provisioning delays.

alex: Good call. Another wrinkle: VPA is set to recommendations mode for the same deployment and sometimes triggers pod restarts when memory recommendations apply, which confuses scaling as pods restart while CA is still provisioning nodes. Restart storms + CA lag = tail latency spikes.

sam: We should separate concerns: GPU-bound inference deployments should have VPA disabled (or set to "off") and use explicit resource requests/limits tuned via Optimize. VPA restarts are harmful when you rely on fast scale-ups.

maria: Also saw this metric-adapter error in logs: `error fetching metric redis_queue_length: value is NaN`. When custom-metrics reports NaN HPA treats it as 0 and can scale down unexpectedly. Posting snippet: ```time="2026-03-02T09:12:11Z" level=error msg="metrics adapter: value NaN for redis_queue_length"```

priya: That adapter error could be from a transient Redis outage or our metric exporter hitting a 429. We should add retry and default handling so HPA doesn't interpret NaN as 0.

alex: Proposed mitigation steps: 1) Add a small warm pool of 1-2 standby GPU nodes in each critical region (non-preemptible), 2) Switch HPA to scale conservatively (use average over 60s), 3) Disable VPA for inference deployments, 4) Add KEDA with a Redis scaler + cooldown, 5) Fix metrics-adapter NaN handling. Thoughts?

sam: Cost tradeoff on warm pool: ~0.5-1 GPU node per region will add $Xk/month. But it buys sub-second cold-start for pods. Maybe make it optional per customer tier (enterprise gets warm nodes).

maria: For immediate triage I can flip VPA to off on the affected deployment and lower HPA aggressiveness. I'll also add a metric alert when adapter returns NaN > 30s.

priya: I'll open a CA issue: investigate expander settings and cloud instance provisioning times; maybe switch to a different instance family that boots faster in the region. Also check k8s pod topology spread rules — if anti-affinity forces pods to different zones and only one zone has GPUs, CA will overprovision.

alex: One more gotcha we found: taints/tolerations mismatch. Some older nodepool configs used `gpu:present:NoSchedule` and newer pods only tolerate `nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule`. That caused CA to create nodes that pods couldn't schedule on. I pushed a checklist to infra runbook.

sam: Thanks. Action items: Maria flips VPA off + HPA smoothing (PR 3487), Priya files CA perf issue, Alex adds warm-pool proposal for tiering, I'll propose a cost vs latency spreadsheet.

infra-bot: Deploybot: PR 3487 merged to staging by maria at 1793512700.

maria: Deployed to staging. Initial test: queue spike -> pods created, staging warm node absorbed pods instantly, 95p latency back to baseline. Moving to prod change after smoke. :rocket:

alex: Nice. Let's keep monitor on for 48h and revisit cost numbers after.

priya: +1. I'll add a grafana panel for NaN-rate and node provisioning time.

sam: Thanks team. Worth documenting in eng-infra runbook and flagging for Dedicated customer SLAs. :+1:
